0.original: <hex:024804F201FC03><hex:024904F201FD03> Quest Sync<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103><hex:02100103>Row-rooth has something to ask you.

48.original: I have a question─one that can only be answered by a being of flesh and bone. Will you hear it?

49.original: Thank you. Before I ask, however, I require that you learn more of my kind, lest your answer be senseless and vapid.

50.original: You can come to know us through our final words─though, alas, you cannot comprehend them in your corporeal form.

51.original: Thus, I shall temporarily free you from your body, allowing you to perceive as we Ea do. Please indicate when you are ready to shuffle off your mortal coil.

52.original: You have prepared, yes? Very well. After you have been liberated, I ask that you read three epitaphs ere returning to me.

53.original: Please brace yourself, as there is the recorded evidence that this may “feel weird”...

54.original: In order to progress, you must complete the objectives while transfigured.

55.original: You will return from your transfigured status if you move too far away. Look to your map for the transfiguration's area of effect.

56.original: If necessary, speak with Row-rooth to restore the transfiguration.

57.original: I ask that you read three epitaphs, then return to me.

58.original: Tragically, your spirit has re-entered your body. Permit me to free you once more.

59.original: Something is written here in an unfamiliar script. You cannot read it as you are.

60.original: In order to progress, you must be under the transfigured status.

61.original: (-Epitaph-)I grasp eternity, yet I hold only loss.<hex:02100103>If forever has an end,<hex:02100103>Why has it not come?

62.original: (-Epitaph-)We fought to go beyond our star;<hex:02100103>We fought to go beyond our dimension;<hex:02100103>We fought for nothing.

63.original: (-Epitaph-)With no future, we turn to the past,<hex:02100103>Knowing none have turned to our present.<hex:02100103>We are the dead end.

64.original: You have read them? This is well. However, you have yet to look upon our most important text. Please seek it in the charming wooded area outside our home.

65.original: Please seek our most important text amidst the memory of trees. I do not know how to make this any clearer.

66.original: (-Epitaph-)The price of eternity is joy;<hex:02100103>Its gift, unending sorrow.

67.original: So you have read all that was left behind...

68.original: Those inscriptions were written by the first of our kind. The first to know the pinnacle of enlightenment, and the first to know the depths of despair.

69.original: They have prepared you to answer my question. As someone bound to a corporeal form, do you think there is hope to be found in life?

72.original: The only way to know is to keep living.

73.original: Strange... But perhaps it is precisely that spongy form which allows you to cling to the intangible unto death. How fortunate for you.

74.original: Fascinating... It must be precisely that spongy form which allows you to cling to the intangible unto death. How fortunate for you.

75.original: Fascinating... It appears that embarking on that quest for hope and seeing it to its ultimate conclusion is a sort of corporeal privilege.

76.original: Fascinating... Though your flesh is spongy and weak, it gives you the strength to live in pursuit of hope.

77.original: That was most edifying. Creatures of flesh enjoy shiny tokens, do they not? Please have some as thanks.

78.original: ...Ah, yes. I shall return you to your body, as it seems you are fond of it.
